title: PORTE LOUIS XV AU PALAIS D'ÉTÉ (p. 377), Pl. XII (printed caption)
date: Plate in Favier, c. 1897 (Rijksmuseum, book); same negative as Child's Princes Porch, 1875-77 per the Commons text on P0194
creator: Thomas Child, by match with P0193/P0194 (Favier names no photographer); plate signed K. OGAWA lower right, read on the image
licence: Rijksmuseum data API: CC0 1.0 on the digital image, Public Domain Mark 1.0 on the record
attribution: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (CC0)
why: Same negative as Child's Princes Porch (P0193, P0194), branch for branch with the same fallen lintel and plaster losses; its form is the side gate of 观水法 Guan Shuifa on plate P0056, and no other of the 20 plates has it. Same picture, by eye, as Teng Gu 1933 fig.15 (S871), which he captions 觀水法正面側翼之一門, a side gate of the 观水法 wing, and copies from Favier, whom he cites at p.264 against P0709's p.377 (edition or pagination not resolved). Second-hand caption, so the coordinator may keep likely. No new row: no new view.
also_shows: 西洋楼 by style; gate not identified
notes: Replaces the first pass's row with no shows. Not a new view: a retouched, cropped print of Child's negative, so it records the 1870s, not the 1890s; the catalogue's Commons tie (XY11:likely) stands and this adds a CC0 holder copy, sharper in the ornament. Compared at full size with P0044 花园门北面, P0047 养雀笼东面, P0057 线法山门, P0059 线法山东门: all differ (columns, balustrade, three-bay screens). Plate P0056 agrees on: arch on two panelled piers, shell cartouches in the spandrels and over the arch, scale fringe under the cornice, steps up to the gate. It differs on one point: the cornice is an S-curve here and nearly gabled on the plate, hence likely and not sure. East or west gate not argued. These gates have no ids. Favier's text pp. 377-381 (archive.org pkinghistoireetd00favi, Getty Research Institute copy, plain text read) does not name the gate: 'Louis XV' is his style label only.
